newsitem.title: USA: Perry cites danger of North Korea spasm.
newsitem.headline: Perry cites danger of North Korea spasm.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Saturday that communist-ruled North Korea was in danger of disintegrating and this could spark a "spasmodic response."

Perry, in comments taped for broadcast on CNN's "Evans & Novak" programme, said the North's rulers had tended to lose control and authority in the last few years while their military clout had declined.

"And there is a danger, I think, of the disintegration which could lead to some sort of a spasmodic response," he added. "I say there is a danger and you have to pay very, very close attention to North Korea."

Perry did not spell out what he meant by a spasmodic response, but earlier this month John Deutch, then-director of central intelligence, predicted in Senate testimony the North either was headed for war with South Korea, would collapse or be on the path to reunification within three years.
Perry said the North continued to deploy two thirds of its million-man army near the demilitarized zone that has separated the North and South since an uneasy truce ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
"So this is a situation that I put very -- right up near the top of the radar screen," he said. "And we have to watch very, very carefully."
